item.title: [SwiftHFR] Drafts file: v1 format pinned by a golden test; one unreadable entry no longer sets the file aside (#1183)
item.body:
Closes #1183
Claim: cloud/m4q-reliab-opus
Author model: Opus 5.5 (cloud/m4q-reliab-opus)
Reviewer model: Fable 5.2 (cloud/m4q-reliab-opus-review-1183-r1, -r2, -r3; APPROVE on 0a49db6a)

**Problem.** `drafts.json` is keyed by `DraftContext`'s synthesized `Codable`, so case and label names are on-disk keys, and no test held a literal file. A later rename would keep every round trip green, and on upgrade each member's `drafts.json` would fail to decode and be set aside: all drafts and archived replies gone. One bad entry already set the whole file aside (`DraftStore.loadedState`, `catch is DecodingError`).

**Change.**
- **Golden v1 file** (`DraftFileFormatTests`): one draft per `DraftContext` case, with both archived sources (`quote`, `quickReply`), captured from the writer at 1b6f98f0. It covers the nested `TopicID`, `CategoryID` (`"13"`, `"prive"`) and `ArchivedDraftSource` codings.
  - `readsTheVersion1FileOfEveryContext`: the file reads back to the expected drafts.
  - `writesTheVersion1File`: the writer still produces that file, compared as parsed JSON.
- **Entry by entry**: `DraftDocument` reads its drafts one by one and counts the entries it cannot read (a newer build's context, a malformed date) in `unreadableEntryCount`. When there are any, the store:
  - copies the file as it was aside, byte for byte (`drafts.json.corrupt`, same rotation as a quarantine, never deleted, and not copied again if `.corrupt` already holds these bytes);
  - writes the readable drafts back and loads them;
  - tells the member once (`didRecoverFromCorruptData`).
- **Safety**:
  - If the copy or the write fails, writes stay blocked, as for an I/O failure, so no save can drop an entry that was not set aside.
  - `DraftPersistence.backUpUnreadableData()` refuses by default. `FileDraftPersistence` copies, and `InMemoryDraftPersistence` is an explicit no-op.
- **Unchanged**: a file that is not a draft document at all, or a newer version, is still set aside whole, as before.
- **`page`**: it stays in `.reply` because it is in the key and in the v1 file. A comment says the app always writes 1.
- **Explicit `DraftContext` coding**: not done. The synthesized coding is the v1 format, and the golden test pins it. A comment says a format change needs a new `currentVersion` with a migration on read.
- **Docs**: LOT-063 §Format is updated. LOT-157 now says the drafts' `.corrupt` copies keep an erased account's texts, as every store's set-aside data does.

**Tests** (HFRKit, run on Linux):
- `anUnreadableEntryIsSetAsideNotTheFile` and `aBadDateIsOneUnreadableEntry` were red before the change (the file was set aside).
- `anEntryThatCannotBeSetAsideBlocksWrites`, `aPersistenceWithoutABackupBlocksWrites` and `aRetriedSetAsideKeepsOneCopy` each go red under their mutation (checked by the author and the reviewer).
- The two golden tests pass by design: they fail on any later format change.
- Full `swift test` green: 2184 tests. SwiftLint 0.65.1 `--strict` clean.

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Fable 5.2, cloud/m4q-reliab-opus-review-1183-r1, round 1): REQUEST CHANGES** — head 91547b16

1. **High** — `DraftStore.swift:113-122` and `:58-61` with `DraftDocument.swift:18`. Erasing an account leaves its unreadable entries on disk, text included. Probe: golden file plus one unknown-context entry of `user1`; `discardAll(account: "user1")` returns 6, the file still holds that entry and `accountKeys()` is `[]`, so `AccountDataEraser` reports success and "leftovers" never offers it. With only unreadable entries nothing is written at all. Fix: `discardAll` also removes raw entries whose `account` is the key (and those with no readable `account`), `accountKeys()` lists them; add a test.
2. **Medium** — `DraftDocument.swift:54-55`. Unreadable entries are never expired or bounded. Probe: 500 entries dated 2001, `maximumCount: 5`, `save` then `purgeExpired()`: 500 remain, rewritten on every save. Fix: expire on a readable `updatedAt`, cap the count, drop what has neither.
3. **Medium** — `DraftFileFormatTests.swift:20`. The golden file pins `source: "quote"` only. Mutation `case quickReply = "quick"`: every Draft and ArchivedReplies test stays green, which is #1183's scenario for the replies set aside from the composer. Fix: a second `archivedReply` entry with `quickReply`.
4. **Low** — `DraftDocument.swift:6-8`, `LOT-063-drafts.md:27`. "Kept as written" is false for numbers: `18446744073709551615` is written back as `1.8446744073709552e+19`, `-0.0` as `0`, a duplicate key is lost. Fix: say so, or keep the entry's text.
5. **Detail** — `DraftFileFormatTests.swift:70`. The test is named `…DropsOneDraft…` while the entry is kept; nothing asserts that the bad-date entry is written back.

Accepted: synthesized `DraftContext` coding pinned by the golden test, `page` kept with its comment, entries kept raw (subject to 1 and 2).

**Verified** (Linux, scratch copy of the head): `swift test --filter Draft` green; on base `DraftDocument.swift` the two golden tests pass and `anUnknownContextDropsOneDraftNotTheFile` and `aBadDateIsOneUnreadableEntry` fail; probes above; SwiftLint clean on both `Drafts` folders. Not compiled: the app target (no `DraftDocument(` call or memberwise use found in `App/`).

comments.body:
Round 1 handled in 30d7f308 by changing the design, not by patching raw entries.

- **Findings 1, 2 and 4.** Unreadable entries no longer live in the file. A file with unreadable entries is copied aside byte for byte (`drafts.json.corrupt`, the same place and rotation as a quarantine, never deleted). The readable drafts are then written back and loaded, and the member is told once (`didRecoverFromCorruptData`).
  - Deletion, expiry and the size bound only ever see readable drafts, and nothing is re-encoded, so numbers and duplicate keys cannot change.
  - If the copy or the write fails, writes stay blocked, as for an I/O failure, so no save can drop an entry that was not set aside (`anEntryThatCannotBeSetAsideBlocksWrites`).
  - A deleted account's unreadable entry therefore ends up in a `.corrupt` copy, like any file set aside. LOT-157 already documents that `.corrupt` copies keep their bytes ("the bytes stay in the `.corrupt` copy"), and the account deletion does not erase them. That is an existing property of every quarantine, not new here.
  - `DraftPersistence.backUpUnreadableData()` has a no-op default for in-memory stores and test doubles.
- **Finding 3.** The golden file now holds a second `archivedReply` with `source: "quickReply"`.
- **Finding 5.** The test is renamed `anUnreadableEntryIsSetAsideNotTheFile`. Both unreadable-entry tests now check that the `.corrupt` copy equals the original bytes, that the rewritten file holds the readable drafts, and that the next load is clean.
- LOT-063 §Format and the `DraftContext` comment are updated.

`swift test`: 2182 tests green. SwiftLint `--strict` clean.

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Fable 5.2, cloud/m4q-reliab-opus-review-1183-r2, round 2)**: APPROVE — head 30d7f308

No blocking finding. The production path (`FileDraftPersistence` behind `ComposerServices.liveDrafts`) does what the spec asks. Round-1 findings 1, 3, 4 and 5 are resolved; finding 2 becomes finding 2 below.

1. **Low** — `Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRStorage/Drafts/DraftPersistence.swift:15-18`. The no-op default of `backUpUnreadableData()` breaks the invariant written at `DraftStore.swift:189-191`. Probe: a wrapper forwarding `load`/`save`/`quarantine` to a `FileDraftPersistence` without implementing the backup drops the unknown entry, leaves no `.corrupt`, and `didRecoverFromCorruptData()` is true. No such conformer exists in production today. Fix: make it a requirement, or have the default throw with an explicit no-op in `InMemoryDraftPersistence`.
2. **Low** — `FileDraftPersistence.swift:36-41`. Each load whose write-back fails adds a full copy. Probe: copy succeeds, save throws, three `reload()` calls leave four `.corrupt*` files. The same happens after a crash between copy and save. Fix: skip the copy when `.corrupt` already has the file's bytes (`contentsEqual`).
3. **Low (docs)** — `docs/lots/LOT-157-account-deletion.md:62` covers reading positions only. After a set-aside, `discardAll` removes 7 drafts and `accountKeys()` is empty, but the `.corrupt` copy still holds the erased account's readable texts. This matches the whole-file quarantine on `dev-swift`, so it is not a regression. Say it for drafts.
4. **Detail** — stale comments: `DraftStore.swift:6-8` ("the store starts empty"), `DraftStore.swift:75`, `App/SwiftHFR/Composer/ReplyComposerModel.swift:147`. `unreadableEntryCount` is a public init parameter and part of `==`.

**Verified**
- `swift test --filter Draft` on Linux at 30d7f308: 47 tests pass.
- Mutation, strict entry decoding: `anUnreadableEntryIsSetAsideNotTheFile`, `aBadDateIsOneUnreadableEntry` and `anEntryThatCannotBeSetAsideBlocksWrites` go red.
- Mutation, file backup removed: the two `.corrupt` byte checks go red.
- Probes for findings 1 to 3.
- `swiftlint` on the changed files: clean.
- Read only: the notice wording fits the partial case; no App double wraps a file persistence.
- Not run: App tests and the Darwin `copyItem` path (macOS only).

---

comments.body:
Round 2's non-blocking findings are handled in 0a49db6a. It is a new head, so a last review runs on it.

1. `backUpUnreadableData()` now throws by default, so the store blocks writes. `InMemoryDraftPersistence` has an explicit no-op. Test: `aPersistenceWithoutABackupBlocksWrites` (a wrapper that forwards everything but the backup leaves the file untouched).
2. No copy is made when `.corrupt` already holds the file's bytes. Test: `aRetriedSetAsideKeepsOneCopy`. Without the check it was red, with five files after three `reload()` calls.
3. LOT-157 now says the drafts' `.corrupt` copies keep an erased account's texts, as every store's set-aside data does.
4. The `DraftStore` header and the notice comments in `DraftStore` and `ReplyComposerModel` are updated. `unreadableEntryCount` in `==` is harmless: the store resets it to 0 before it keeps the document.

`swift test`: 2184 green. SwiftLint `--strict` clean.

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Fable 5.2, cloud/m4q-reliab-opus-review-1183-r3, round 3)**: APPROVE — head 0a49db6a

No blocking finding. The commit does what round 2 asked and adds nothing wrong.

1. **Detail** — `Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRStorage/Drafts/InMemoryDraftPersistence.swift:29`: the comment says a document in memory holds no unreadable entry, but the public `DraftDocument(unreadableEntryCount:)` initialiser can seed one. Harmless (the count is a number, no entry is lost; the store only raises the notice). No fix required.

**Checked**
- Throwing default vs app test doubles (by reading; the app target does not build on Linux): `CountingDraftPersistence`, `UnreadableDraftPersistence` and `FailingDraftPersistence` never return a document with `unreadableEntryCount > 0`. The count is only set by decoding a file or by the explicit initialiser, which no app or package test uses; the store only saves documents with count 0, and the count is never encoded. So none of them reaches the throw. No other `DraftPersistence` conformer exists in `App/`.
- `FileManager.contentsEqual`: a missing `.corrupt` gives false (first-time path, covered by the existing tests). A directory named `drafts.json.corrupt` gives false, is moved to a unique name, then the copy is made (local probe test, green on Linux). A partial copy differs, so it is kept and a new one is made.
- Mutations (scratch copy): default backup made a no-op again → `aPersistenceWithoutABackupBlocksWrites` red; `contentsEqual` skip disabled → `aRetriedSetAsideKeepsOneCopy` red. Both green on the unmodified head.
- `swift test --filter Draft` on Linux: 49 tests green.
- `swiftlint lint --strict` at the repository root: exit 0. `ReplyComposerModel.swift` is 397 lines; no line over 140 in the touched files.
- Docs: the LOT-157 line matches the code (the erase rewrites `drafts.json`, `.corrupt` copies are untouched); `DraftStore` header and notice comments match the behaviour; no stale mention of the old no-op default.

Not run: the app tests (macOS only), left to CI.
